How to fix it

Round the sharp inside corner to a 1.5 mm radius
Stress piles up in the sharp inside corner. A fillet of 1.5 mm (about half the 3 mm wall) spreads it out.
Switch to PLA (3D printed)
Stress stays about the same for the same shape and load, so PLA (3D printed) (50 MPa) gives safety factor 5.70. It is 1.5x as stiff, so deflection scales by 0.671. Other options: PETG (3D printed) (5.36), ABS (3D printed) (3.76).

Setup

materialPolycarbonate
limit62 MPa
target safety factor2
mass48.55 g
load120 N down @ top and within 8 of 25,15,28
fixturefixed z=min
part4 holes, 1 inside fillets, 30 sharp inside corners, walls about 3 mm

Assumptions

  1. Linear elastic material and small deflections (no yielding redistribution, no buckling).
  2. Polycarbonate: E 2350 MPa, Poisson 0.37, von Mises vs yield 62 MPa (Covestro Makrolon 2405 datasheet).
  3. Loads are static and applied all at once; no impact, vibration or fatigue.
  4. Molded part treated as isotropic and uniform; weld lines and the area near the gate can be weaker than the datasheet.
  5. Fixed faces are perfectly rigid; real mounts flex a little, which lowers peak stress next to them.
  6. Contact between separate parts, friction and preload are not modeled.

Notes

  • Built from enclosure.py with wall=3, length=90, width=60, height=28, corner=6, boss=7.
  • A coarser first mesh folded on the thin walls, so the study starts from the finer one (114,014 nodes).
  • Thin walls need a large first mesh (114,014 nodes), so this study takes longer than usual.
Made with Wobbl 0.1.0. Solver CalculiX 2.23. Total time 270 s.
